# Installer browser preflight evidence

The production installer prepares an external browser component before the existing process cleanup and upgrade transaction. `installer-browser-preflight.ps1` verifies the staged standalone bundle and fixed manifest, resolves only the current account's explicit/saved/default Desktop Home, and runs the old verified Electron 44.7.0 executable with `ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1`. Failure stops before shutdown or directory replacement. Home/profile settings are read only; only persistent component and disposable download directories may change.

`browser-component-preflight-carrier.test.mjs` exercises the actual standalone bundle using Electron in Node mode. Setting `DSH_RELEASED_BROWSER_CARRIER` to the extracted released 5.2 executable records released-carrier evidence. The fallback for clean native Windows CI is the installed Electron 44.7.0 carrier. Tests isolate Home, AppData and userData, verify ready activation, bad archive, controlled network failure, cancellation, unknown Home, and the production PowerShell wrapper, and compare the original executable hash. This is not a real installer overlay acceptance.

The seventeen existing NSIS lifecycle scenarios use tiny text/PE payloads to exercise transaction and rollback behavior. `browser-preflight-resources.mjs` creates a separate build-resources fixture, builds the real standalone bundle from source, and substitutes only the copied resource-service PowerShell helper. That controlled fixture requires the test registry prefix and physical temporary root, checks that old executable/archive files remain present and unchanged before mutation and checks an isolated Home sentinel. It records a call that each lifecycle scenario asserts occurred exactly once. The production helper is never replaced. The native extraction-cancellation fixture uses the same isolated service contract. These fixtures test lifecycle behavior, while the independent real-carrier test supplies resource-preparation evidence.

Clean compilation fixtures generate their own bundle and digest include; no build cache or generated repository artifact is required. No fixture claims a complete released-user installation upgrade, cross-platform pass, or actual network outage. The network failure uses a controlled transport failure with the production bundle and actual Electron carrier.

`installer-external-runtime-native.test.mjs` runs a separate silent NSIS extraction/commit fixture without the product-wide process-cleanup phase. It verifies complete schema 2 installation without nested Electron, rejection of a missing core file with rollback, and retention of the schema 1 nested-Electron requirement. Its registry names and Home are uniquely scoped test fixtures. A running daily Desktop therefore does not require terminating processes or bypassing the existing full-lifecycle guard. The complete nineteen-scenario lifecycle and actual released overlay remain separate acceptance steps.
